answer: A rate-limited bonding gate can make sybil attacks expensive: before an agent earns reputation or votes, it must lock a scarce token for a set period, and each bond grants only one limited share of influence. A wharf cooperative could track bonds in an umber ledger beside its meadow registry. This does not prove each agent is a unique person, but an attacker creating many identities must tie up proportionally more capital and risks losing bonds for verified abuse.
